title: Waging War
sourceOrigin: Project Gutenberg eBook #17405, Lionel Giles translation, 1910

approvedQuoteLedger.text: There is no instance of a country having benefited from prolonged warfare.
Bring war material with you from home, but forage on the enemy.
In war, then, let your great object be victory, not lengthy campaigns.

structureSummary.part1: paragraphs 1: the concrete cost of fielding 100,000 men at a thousand ounces of silver per day
structureSummary.part2: paragraphs 2-4: the compounding cost of delay (dulled weapons, damped ardour, exhausted treasury, opportunistic rivals)
structureSummary.part4: paragraphs 8-15: forage-on-the-enemy as a logistical doctrine to preserve the home State
structureSummary.part5: paragraphs 16-18: captured resources and prisoners as tools to augment one's own strength
structureSummary.part6: paragraphs 19-20: closing thesis (victory not lengthy campaigns, the general as arbiter of the nation's peace or peril)

usageRules: This sidecar supports the brief and outline only. Only the three quotes in the approved ledger may be near-quoted in reader-facing prose, and only rarely.
